tagline: Through the chaparral from Monterey to the Salinas River.
intro: Highway 68 leaves Highway 1 near the Monterey County Fairgrounds as the Monterey-Salinas Highway and heads inland past the airport and Del Rey Oaks, then out through the hills by Laguna Seca, Laureles Grade, Corral de Tierra, San Benancio and Toro Park toward the Salinas River. It is a state scenic route on account of the chaparral, and the lupine that comes up in spring.

In the 1950s and 1960s the state meant to make it a freeway, until environmental concerns stopped the plan. Only short pieces were built, one of them the last three miles toward Spreckels, opened in 1967 on new bridges that replaced an 1889 truss over the Salinas River.

moments.title: Laguna Seca
moments.text: The raceway went in in 1957 around a dry lake bed on part of Fort Ord, its young architect drawing the line in the dirt and walking it for the bulldozers.

moments.title: Corral de Tierra
moments.text: John Steinbeck and his sister Mary played as children at the foot of Castle Rock, the earthen fence that named the valley, and he set The Pastures of Heaven here.

moments.title: Spreckels
moments.text: The town was built to house workers at a sugar beet plant that ran from 1899 to 1982, and Steinbeck lived and worked here for a time.
